preamble: Debuccalization of the voiceless uvular stop [q] to the glottal fricative [h]: the oral (dorsal-uvular) closure is lost while the voiceless laryngeal setting remains. It occurs historically in western Malayo-Polynesian, where Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *q (reconstructed as a uvular stop) became h in the Malayo-Chamic languages (Proto-Malayic *hati, Proto-Chamic *hujaːn) and in Sundanese, while it became ʔ or zero elsewhere (Javanese udan, Balinese ujan 'rain', Tagalog atay 'liver').

examples.note: Proto-Malayic *hati continues PMP *qatay with initial *q > h; compare Tagalog and Cebuano atay, where *q was lost.
Proto-Malayic *hujan; the same *q > h correspondence recurs in initial position across the Malayic lexicon.
Sundanese shares the h reflex of *q with Malay, whereas neighbouring Javanese has udan and Balinese ujan without h.
Old Javanese kept PMP *q as h in many words; modern Javanese has udan (rain) < *quzan without h.
